passage: Every night in the flat went the same way. Bath, pyjamas, then Lalremsiami climbed into her mother Nandini's lap for the rhyme about the little moon. Papa switched off the big light and left the yellow lamp on. Lalremsiami touched Papa's nose, then her mother's, then found the corner of her blanket. When Papa skipped the last line, she frowned until he added it. By the second verse her eyes were closing.

qa.q: What did Papa leave on after switching off the big light?
qa.a: Papa left the yellow lamp on.

qa.q: Why did Lalremsiami frown when Papa skipped the last line?
qa.a: Lalremsiami seems upset when the routine changes, wanting it exactly as it always goes, so the missing line feels wrong.

qa.q: What might help Lalremsiami settle if the family is away from home?
qa.a: The family could keep the same bath, rhyme and blanket corner, and switch the light in the same order, so bedtime still feels the same.

qa.q: What might Nandini feel when Lalremsiami's eyes close during the second verse?
qa.a: Nandini probably feels calm and content, since the familiar routine has done its work. 🙂

grounding: A toddler settles more easily with the same rhyme and order each night, so the family feels like a safe place.

passage: “Hands first, Damini,” said Vandana, lifting her toward the sink. “Wash, wash!” “Wash!” Damini splashed. “Now the blue bowl.” Nani sat down next to the cushion. “Sit, sit.” Damini climbed onto her cushion, patted it twice and waited. “Same song?” asked Nani. “Yum yum,” said Damini, and Vandana began the little eating song. On the last note Damini opened her mouth wide, as she did every time.

qa.q: What did Damini pat twice before waiting?
qa.a: Damini patted her cushion twice.

qa.q: Why does Damini pat the cushion and wait before eating?
qa.a: Damini seems to know the mealtime order well and finds comfort in it, so she waits for the song that comes next.

qa.q: What could Vandana do if Damini gets upset at a mealtime somewhere new?
qa.a: Vandana could bring the blue bowl, wash hands first and sing the same song, so the sequence is as familiar as at home.

qa.q: What might Nani be feeling when Nani asks, “Same song?”
qa.a: Nani probably feels warm and pleased to share the familiar routine with Damini, asking as part of the ritual.

grounding: A toddler follows the same mealtime sequence and song each day, which makes the family feel like a safe place.

passage: Nanny's note for Nazia, Tuesday. Vasudha fought her nap again until I did it your way: curtains, then the blue blanket, then 'Chanda mama' twice. By the second song she was sucking her thumb and holding the blanket corner. She was asleep before 1:30. At lunch she refused rice until I put it in her own steel bowl with the elephant. Will keep the same order tomorrow 🙂

qa.q: Which song did the nanny sing twice?
qa.a: 'Chanda mama'.

qa.q: What does Vasudha holding the blanket corner and sucking her thumb suggest?
qa.a: She was feeling calm and safe once the familiar order of curtains, blanket and song was followed.

qa.q: What is the nanny planning, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Keeping the same order tomorrow, because Vasudha settles when each step is predictable.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel reading the note?
qa.a: Likely relieved and pleased that Nazia's routine works even when Nazia is away, so Vasudha feels at home with the nanny too.

grounding: A toddler settles for sleep and meals when the same familiar sequence is followed.

passage: In their village house, dinner always went the same way for little Yash. Aaji rang the brass bell at the tulsi, everyone sat on the floor, and Yash climbed into his sister Nandini's lap. One ball of dal-rice for the cow, one for the crow, one for Yash. One night Nandini was away at a wedding, and Yash cried and pushed his plate away. Aaji rang the bell. He stopped, watched, and opened his mouth for the crow's bite.

qa.q: Where did Yash usually sit at dinner?
qa.a: In his sister Nandini's lap.

qa.q: Why did Yash cry and push his plate away?
qa.a: He felt upset and unsettled because Nandini was away and the usual dinner order was broken.

qa.q: What did Aaji do that helped, and why did it work?
qa.a: She rang the brass bell, a familiar first step, which told Yash dinner was happening the usual, safe way.

qa.q: How might Nandini feel hearing about that night?
qa.a: She might feel touched that her part mattered so much, and glad Aaji knew how to keep the routine going.

grounding: A toddler relies on a familiar mealtime sequence, and a familiar step helps him settle when part of it changes.

passage: Every night in their flat in Lagos, Ada's bedtime went in the same order: bath, pyjamas with stars, then Mummy Nkechi's song about the sleeping moon, while Daddy switched off the big light and her brother Chidera whispered 'Goodnight, Ada' from the top bunk. The night the power went out, everything was dark and wrong. Ada wailed. Mummy lit a lamp and sang the moon song anyway. Chidera whispered his line. Ada's sobs slowed. She tucked her toy rabbit under her chin and closed her eyes.

qa.q: What did Ada tuck under her chin?
qa.a: Her toy rabbit.

qa.q: Why did Ada wail when the power went out?
qa.a: She was frightened and unsettled because the dark changed the usual bedtime order.

qa.q: What helped Ada settle, even in the dark?
qa.a: Mummy Nkechi singing the same moon song and Chidera whispering his line, so the routine stayed the same.

qa.q: How might Chidera feel whispering his line in the dark?
qa.a: He may feel proud and grown-up, helping calm his little sister with his part of the routine.

grounding: A toddler settles at bedtime through the same family sequence, even when the power goes out.

passage:
Monday: new flat, new room. Francis, two, cried at bedtime and kicked his blanket off three times. Papa Anand tried a new storybook; Francis pushed it away.
Wednesday: Anand went back to the old way: bath, the same blue cup of milk, Mama switching off the big light, and the moon song, twice. Francis hummed along through a yawn.
Saturday: at the first line of the moon song, Francis climbed into bed by himself and patted the pillow for Papa.

qa.q: What song did Anand sing at bedtime?
qa.a: Anand sang the moon song, twice.

qa.q: Why did Francis push the new storybook away on Monday?
qa.a: He was probably unsettled and upset in the new room, and a new story felt strange rather than comforting.

qa.q: What helped Francis settle, and why?
qa.a: Going back to the same bath, blue cup, light and moon song made bedtime predictable, so Francis felt safe.

qa.q: What might bedtime be like for Anand once the routine works?
qa.a: He is likely relieved and feels close to Francis, since bedtime is now calm instead of a struggle.

grounding: Shows a toddler settling more easily once the same bedtime sequence returns each night, making the new home feel safe.
